_meta.description: Per-country standards for indoor geolocation (plugs, mains, currencies, languages, calling codes, calendar/clock/units conventions, driving side, emergency numbers). Keys are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.mains_notes: Bathrooms may have shaver supply units.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.mains_notes: Live and neutral reversed compared to Chinese and Australian/NZ Type I.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.mains_notes: In some areas, a 3×230 V three-phase delta system is used with no neutral conductor, so domestic single-phase loads are connected across two phases. While this works fine for most appliances, it can cause problems with electric-vehicle chargers that often require a neutral conductor physically bonde

BQ.name: Caribbean Netherlands
BQ.mains_notes: Sockets for 220–240 V European Type C plugs are typically available at hotels ; some buildings modify voltage, so travellers are advised to check before plugging in. ; Type F are also available at some hotels.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.mains_notes: Before standardization, socket types varied: C (very old installations), I (for air conditioners), and combinations like A/C and A/B/C.

CA.name: Canada
CA.mains_notes: NEMA 5-20R outlets, which are similar to Type B but have a T-shaped neutral slot, are sometimes used for higher current 120 V equipment (up to 20 A). Homes are typically provided with 120/240 V split-phase power ; NEMA 14-30R and 14-50R receptacles are provided on 240 V circuits for clothes dryers a

CL.name: Chile
CL.mains_notes: Type L is the official national standard ; Europlugs (Type C) are compatible. Schuko (Type F) plugs are often used for high power appliances.

CN.name: China
CN.mains_notes: Type C no longer meets national standards since GB/T 1002-2021 came into effect ; firms stopped producing, selling or installing Type C and A/C hybrid sockets, but A/C hybrid sockets can still be found in legacy installations.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.mains_notes: NEMA 5-20R outlets, which are similar to Type B but have a T-shaped neutral slot, are sometimes used for higher current 120 V commercial equipments (up to 20 A). On the other hand, NEMA 10-50P outlets are sometimes used for 208 V and 240 V industrial equipments (up to 50 A).

CU.name: Cuba
CU.mains_notes: Some modern hotels have 220 V sockets for European 2-pin plugs (Type C).

CW.name: Curaçao
CW.mains_notes: Some hotels and apartments have 220 V European sockets.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.mains_notes: Type E and F sockets are legal but rare ; Type E, F and 7/7 plugs can be inserted into the widespread Type K sockets, but no earth contact is established.

ES.name: Spain
ES.mains_notes: Type E is extremely rare, but it may appear in some buildings, such as the University Carlos III of Madrid. Almost every Spanish plug would work on Type E sockets.

ET.name: Ethiopia
ET.mains_notes: Type E is very rare because Ethiopia never had French influences.

FJ.name: Fiji
FJ.mains_notes: Same plugs and sockets as in Australia.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.mains_notes: Type D mostly historical, nowadays used only for remotely switched lighting and similar. ; Type M historically used in domestic installations, now only for stage lighting (where they are increasingly replaced with Ceeform). Bathrooms may have shaver supply units.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.mains_notes: Type G is the only general purpose outlet type in use in Ireland. Bathrooms may have shaver sockets. These accept 2.5 A Europlug CEE 7/16 and UK type BS 4573 plugs, which are used on shavers and toothbrushes. They do not accept larger Type C plugs and general purpose outlets are generally banned in

IM.name: Isle of Man
IM.mains_notes: Self-governing British crown dependency, but generally uses UK technical standards.

IN.name: India
IN.mains_notes: The combination of a Type C, E or F plug with a Type D socket may often be workable, but it is unsafe to use. From August 2015, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) began clamping down on the sale of imported products with Type C/E/F plugs by pushing manufacturers and importers to comply with the IS

IT.name: Italy
IT.mains_notes: Type L uses two gauges of plug and socket. The 10 A version has pin spacing that is compatible with Europlug. The 16 A version uses wider pin spacing and larger pins. Hybrid outlets that accept both types are common and some also accept Type F. The ungrounded CEE contour plug (CEE 7/17) fits into su

JO.name: Jordan
JO.plug_types_raw: B, C, D, F, G, J

JP.name: Japan
JP.mains_notes: East Japan 50 Hz (Tokyo, Kawasaki, Sapporo, Yokohama, and Sendai) ; West Japan 60 Hz (Okinawa, Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe, Nagoya, and Hiroshima). Most sockets accept only Type A plugs. See Electricity transmission in Japan for more.

KH.name: Cambodia
KH.mains_notes: Modern installations often have universal sockets that accept plugs of most common types, but without establishing earth contact when used with Type E/F plugs (American Type B and British Type G plugs will be properly earthed). Older installations are usually A/C hybrid sockets without earthing.

LA.name: Laos
LA.mains_notes: Some buildings and households have hybrid sockets compatible with Type A, B, and C.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.mains_notes: Type C sockets are the most frequent. Many buildings and households have double use sockets compatible with Type A and C.

LK.name: Sri Lanka
LK.mains_notes: Only Type G permitted to be manufactured or imported from August 2017.

MM.name: Myanmar (Burma)
MM.plug_types_raw: A, C, D, F, G, I

MX.name: Mexico
MX.mains_notes: Both 120/240 V split-phase and 127/220 V three-phase are used.

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.mains_notes: Type G is most common. Devices using a Europlug (Type C) may be sold but require an adaptor, since there are usually no sockets for them. Some power strips accept both Type C and G plugs via slightly wider apertures and modified shutter mechanisms. ; Type M is used mainly for air conditioners and bo

NC.name: New Caledonia
NC.mains_notes: Despite that New Caledonia is a French territory, German Schuko Type F sockets are used instead of French Type E sockets.

NE.name: Niger
NE.plug_types_raw: A, B, C, D, E, F

NO.name: Norway
NO.mains_notes: 230 V on IT grid, and 400 V on TN grid.

PH.name: Philippines
PH.mains_notes: Many buildings and households have double-use sockets compatible with Type A and C, and often also with B for grounded plugs. NEMA 6-15 is used for air conditioners.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.mains_notes: Type E is very rare, used only in very old installations.

PY.name: Paraguay
PY.mains_notes: In 2022, Type N was chosen as new national standard, but so far hybrid A/C or A/B/C sockets are most common.

RU.name: Russia
RU.mains_notes: USSR (along with much of Eastern Europe) used GOST sockets with 4.0 mm pins similar to Type C plugs and the 4.8 mm standard used by Type E and F.

RW.name: Rwanda
RW.mains_notes: Type G is the official standard, adopted to harmonize with the East African Community. Types E sockets are no longer official but remain common in older buildings. The Europlug (Type C) that fits into them (but not officially into Type G sockets) remains in frequent usage too, though there are usual

SE.name: Sweden
SE.mains_notes: Bathrooms may have shaver supply units.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.mains_notes: Type G sockets are most common. ; Type C appliances may be sold, but may require an adaptor for use with these sockets. ; Type M is used mainly for air conditioners and other high-powered equipment. Hotel bathrooms may have shaver supply units.

SH.name: St. Helena, Ascension & Tristan da Cunha

TH.name: Thailand
TH.mains_notes: Hybrid A/B/C sockets are most common ; in addition to American (A, B) and Europlugs (C) they also accept the newly introduced Thai plug (O). Belgian/French and Schuko plugs (E, F) also fit, but no earth contact is established, hence the sale of appliances with E or F plugs has been banned.

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.mains_notes: Sockets in older buildings are often unearthed and accept only Type A plugs. High-power appliances such as air conditioners and ovens may run on 220 V via split-phase.

US.name: United States
US.mains_notes: NEMA 5-20R outlets, which are similar to Type B but have a T-shaped neutral slot, are sometimes used for higher current 120 V equipment (up to 20 A). Homes are typically provided with 120/240 V split-phase power ; NEMA 14-30R and 14-50R receptacles are provided on 240 V circuits for clothes dryers a

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.mains_notes: Type I was the main standard until the 1990s, and still appears in old installations.

VE.name: Venezuela
VE.mains_notes: Both 120/208 V three-phase and 120/240 V split-phase are used.

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.mains_notes: Most households use unearthed hybrid sockets that accept Type A and C plugs. Hybrid sockets that accept Type A, B, and C plugs are sometimes used in commercial installations. ; Type F plugs are frequently plugged into hybrid sockets, though this is somewhat unsafe, as no earth contact is made.
